summary.tagline: The Blasket Islands (Irish: Na Blascaodaí) are an uninhabited group of islands off the west coast of the Dingl

days.title: History and Facilities of Great Blasket
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Siedlung
stops.detail: At the broad and flat eastern end of the island, the remains of the original settlement are located on the hill above the sandy beach.

stops.name: drei erhaltenen Häusern
stops.detail: Overnight stays can be booked in the three preserved houses.

stops.name: Croaghmore
stops.detail: The highest point of the treeless island is “Croaghmore” at 292 m.

stops.name: Sandstrand
stops.detail: The sandy beach at the eastern end of the island, protected by a rocky reef, is an annually recurring birthing ground for seals in summer.

stops.name: Quelle
stops.detail: A spring supplied the settlement with water.

stops.name: Ankerplatz
stops.detail: Sailing ships find a good anchorage at the beach of Great Blasket Island in calm weather.
